interval: 90 % credible interval: median with the lower and upper limits of the 90 % interval (GWOSC API documentation; the catalog papers give symmetric 90 % credible intervals)
format: [median, minus, plus]; null = not released in the event API (shown as unknown)

releases.label: GWTC-1
releases.note: Only GW170817 remains at this version: the GWTC-1 binary black holes were re-analysed in GWTC-2.1.

releases.label: GWTC-2.1
releases.note: Confident O3a events and updated source properties for the binary black holes first reported in GWTC-1 (GWOSC catalog description).

releases.label: GWTC-4.1
releases.note: Confident O4a events, as described in the GWTC-5.0 catalog paper (GWOSC catalog description).

cosmology.note: flat ΛCDM of Ade et al. (2016, Planck 2015, TT+lowP+lensing+ext), used by every release to convert d_L to z and detector-frame to source-frame masses

fields.snr: network matched-filter SNR as shown by the GWOSC event portal (default parameter-estimation result, or the highest search SNR)
fields.far: false-alarm rate (per year), lowest across search pipelines
fields.pa: probability of astrophysical origin, highest across search pipelines

band.note: band-pass of the plotted strain data (§2)

visibleDuration.note: “The entire visible part of the signal lasts for around 0.15s.” (§2)

inspiralBand.note: GW frequencies while the inspiral is visible (§2)

fMax.note: GW frequency at maximum strain amplitude, a “conservative (low) value” (eq. 2)

chirpMass.note: detector frame, adopted from f and ḟ (eq. 7) “for simplicity”; the implied value “remains constant to within 35%” over 30–150 Hz (§2)

chirpMassFit.note: from the slope of a linear fit to f^(−8/3)(t) from zero-crossings (Fig. 3 caption, eq. 8)

separation.note: Keplerian separation at f_max for M = 70 M☉ (eq. 9)

energy.note: E_GW ∼ GMμ/2R down to R = 350 km, a lower-bound estimate (eq. 23)

quotes.text: The GW150914 signal was strong enough to be apparent, without using any waveform model, in the filtered detector strain data.
Note that the characteristic mass scale of the radiating system is obtained by direct inspection of the time-frequency behavior of the observational data.

delay.interval: 68 % (“In this Letter all derived gamma-ray results use 68% confidence levels.”)
delay.note: start of the gamma-ray emission relative to the GW merger time (§2)

distanceUsed.note: “we conservatively use here D = 26 Mpc, the lower bound of the 90% credible interval on luminosity distance derived from the GW signal” (§4.1)

emissionLagAssumed.note: for the lower bound “we assume the SGRB signal was emitted 10 s after the GW signal” (§4.1)

grb.relation: “the fractional speed difference during the trip can be written Δv/v_EM ≈ v_EM Δt/D, where Δv = v_GW − v_EM” (§4.1)

chance.note: probability of the near-simultaneous temporal and spatial observation occurring by chance (abstract)

quotes.text: We therefore confirm binary neutron star mergers as a progenitor of short GRBs.
Standard EM theory minimally coupled to general relativity predicts that GWs and light propagate with identical speeds.

distance.interval: 68.3 % (maximum posterior value with the minimal-width credible interval)
distance.note: GW data alone, sky position fixed to the optical counterpart

tullyFisher.note: distance to NGC 4993 from the Tully–Fisher relation, as quoted (Sakai et al. 2000; Freedman et al. 2001)

groupVelocity.note: CMB-frame recession velocity of the ESO-508 group (Crook et al. 2007), as quoted

bulkFlow.note: coherent bulk-flow correction; standard error 69 km/s, but the more conservative 150 km/s is adopted

H0.interval: 68.3 % (maximum a posteriori and minimal credible interval)
H0.note: Bayesian posterior marginalised over inclination and velocities

quotes.text: This approach does not require any form of cosmic “distance ladder”; the gravitational-wave (GW) analysis can be used to estimate the luminosity distance out to cosmological scales directly, without the use of intermediate astronomical distance measurements.
As vH/c∼1% for GW170817 we do not distinguish between them.
